newsitem.title: USA: Calif economic growth continues in 2nd half - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif economic growth continues in 2nd half - report.

text.p: California's economy has continued to grow at a steady pace in the second half of 1996, according to a state report.

The non-partisan state Legislative Analyst said in the report that wage and salary employment increases have averaged over 30,000 jobs over the past three months, with every major industry sector expect mining experiencing increases.
General fund revenues were up $157 million in October, bringing cumulative receipts for the first four months of this fiscal year to $575 million above the 1996-1997 budget estimate, the report said.

Of the year-to-date gain, $109 million represented a temporary accounting-related gain in trial court revenues, which were expected to be offset in the months ahead. After adjusting for this factor, the Legislative Analyst said the underlying increase in cash receipts came to $466 million.

About $164 million of the $466 million increase was due to unusually large estate tax payments, the report said. The remaining increase -- just over $300 million -- represented the underlying year-to-date gain in 1996-1997 revenue totals, according to the report.
